planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya kentiana blooms most reliably when slightly pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya kentiana has long, narrow, slightly twisted leaves along twining vines, closely resembling its relative Hoya wayetii but with a subtly different leaf shape and twist, and produces rounded clusters of small, star-shaped, deep maroon-red flowers with a sweet fragrance. Its slender, cascading growth suits a hanging basket where the twisting leaves and dangling flower clusters can be appreciated. Provide a trellis or hanging basket for support, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs once they form, since hoya rebloom from the same spurs year after year.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya heuschkeliana blooms most reliably when slightly pot-bound and given bright light.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya heuschkeliana carries small, thick, glossy, closely spaced leaves along fine twining stems, forming a dense, compact vine well suited to a small hanging pot or trained onto a small trellis. Clusters of small, waxy, cream to pale pink star-shaped flowers with a red center appear on reusable flowering spurs, which should never be trimmed off since blooms return from the same spurs each year. Its modest scale and slower growth make it manageable in tighter spaces than larger-leaved hoya species. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and provide bright indirect light for steady growth and reliable flowering.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya davidcummingii is a compact, slow-growing miniature species well suited to small containers.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya davidcummingii is a miniature species with tiny, rounded, dark green leaves densely packed along fine, wiry, trailing stems, giving it a delicate, almost moss-like texture distinct from the larger, thicker leaves of most commonly grown hoya. Small clusters of star-shaped, dark maroon to near-black flowers with a sweet fragrance appear on the reusable flowering spurs, which should never be trimmed off. Its tiny scale suits a small pot or terrarium-style display where larger hoya species would be unmanageable. Let the potting mix dry between waterings and provide bright indirect light for the best growth and flowering.

common_name: Hoya Archboldiana (Large Pink Flowered New Guinea Wax Plant)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix; Hoya archboldiana needs more space than compact hoya species due to its larger leaves and vigorous growth.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging basket in bright, indirect light in fast-draining, chunky potting mix. Hoya archboldiana, native to the mountains of New Guinea, produces large, thick, glossy leaves on vigorous twining vines and is prized for its exceptionally large, showy flower clusters, with individual blooms among the biggest in the genus, opening in shades of deep pink to red with a waxy, substantial texture. Its bold flower size and vigorous growth make it a strong specimen for a large hanging basket or trellis once mature, though it takes longer to reach flowering size than smaller, faster-blooming hoya species. Provide a sturdy support for the twining stems, let the potting mix dry between waterings, and never remove the woody flowering spurs once they form.
